tools.name: open_store
tools.description: Open a new Ripey store for the user. Ask for the store name and the user's email first. Optionally takes the user's Solana wallet address (public address only, never a secret key); in test mode a demo address is used if omitted. Returns the store URL, a private dashboard link, and an agent_key: pass

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List the store's products with their id, price and status (draft or published). Pass the store's agent_key (returned by open_store).

tools.name: create_product
tools.description: Create a DRAFT product in the store. Nothing goes live: show the user the draft (name, description, price) and ask them to approve before calling publish. Pass the store's agent_key (returned by open_store).

tools.name: delete_draft
tools.description: Delete an unpublished draft the user doesn't want. Published products can't be deleted this way. Pass the store's agent_key (returned by open_store).

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Put an approved draft on the store so buyers can purchase it. Only call this after the user approves the draft. Pass the store's agent_key (returned by open_store).

tools.name: checkout_link
tools.description: Return a link where a buyer can purchase a published product (opens the store with the product selected). Pass the store's agent_key (returned by open_store).

tools.name: sales_summary
tools.description: Summarize the store's sales over the last N days (default 7): revenue, orders, customers and top products. Pass the store's agent_key (returned by open_store).

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "open_store" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "create_product" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Create a DRAFT product in the store. Nothing goes live: show the user the draft (name, description, price) and ask them to approve before calling publish. Pass …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: open_store · Private data: open_store · Public sink: open_store, create_product, publish · Destructive: delete_draft.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: open_store · Private data: open_store · Public sink: open_store, create_product, publish · Destructive: delete_draft

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
